title: Authorisation, Capital and the Integration of E-Money
summary: Authorising payment and e-money institutions today, how the reform folds e-money institutions into a single payment institution category, and the reauthorisation, capital and governance implications for existing firms.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Authorising payment and e-money institutions today, how the reform folds e-money institutions into a single payment institution category, and the reauthorisation, capital and governance implications for existing firms.
Learning Objectives: Assess applications against authorisation, capital and fitness requirements
Explain how e-money issuance becomes a payment service under the reform
Plan for reauthorisation and transitional arrangements for existing licence holders
Syllabus: Programme of operations, business plan, governance and own funds methods
A single payment institution category with e-money services
Reauthorisation, transitional periods and grandfathering questions
Agents, distributors, passporting and the narrowing of exclusions
Intended Audience: Authorisation, supervision and policy staff at national competent authorities covering payment and e-money institutions
Compliance, risk, legal, fraud and product staff at payment institutions, e-money institutions and banks
Senior managers and directors of payment firms responsible for regulatory change and transition planning
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of payment services, e-money or their supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 on payment services in the internal market (PSD2)
Directive 2009/110/EC on the taking up, pursuit and prudential supervision of the business of electronic money institutions (Second E-Money Directive)
Regulation (EU) 2024/886 amending Regulations (EU) No 260/2012 and (EU) 2021/1230 and Directives 98/26/EC and (EU) 2015/2366 as regards instant credit transfers in euro (Instant Payments Regulation)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
